data.description:
## Why
An agent sending to a tab must be able to detect the operator’s half-written draft without mistaking Claude’s faint suggestion for user input. Backlog item: A5.

## Evidence
- c11 on origin/main (`0ff8887e5e`): `Sources/TerminalController.swift:6703-6727` pastes then schedules Return with no draft inspection. Its text/submit rules are at `:6662-6697`.
- Upstream: cmux #15302 (`8216c54b52`), `Sources/TerminalController+SurfaceInputState.swift:7-104` reads active-screen styled spans and preserves faint attributes; `cmuxCLITests/CLISendDraftGuardTests.swift:40-150` exercises draft/dialog refusal, empty prompts and unsupported-server behavior.
- Research: Fable “Items the plan bundles” X2; Astra “Missing or hidden work” M1 and §7 item 2; report 03 “Answering: verify, then type”; HTML draft-guard row. BACKLOG A5 admits this only as P2.

## Scope
In: an on-demand bounded input-state primitive (empty, draft, dialog, unknown, with source/freshness) and a send guard that clearly refuses detected drafts/dialogs. Detect faint auto-suggest separately from typed text for fixture-covered prompts.
Out: periodic screen classification, universal TUI recognition, menu-key answering, automatic approvals, blocking hook bridge, changing arbitrary send-key semantics and a claim that an observation guarantees a later keypress is safe.

## Approach
Port the upstream idea, not its mobile-render-grid dependency wholesale. Use an active-screen snapshot with attributes, independent of scrollback viewport; return draft length rather than draft contents. Isolate parsing as a pure bounded function and keep collection to the minimum UI-bound work. Check the resolved target immediately before dispatch where feasible; expose unknown/unavailable honestly. For ordinary send, document the explicit unknown/older-server compatibility policy instead of silently reporting safe. A6 will require a confirmed acceptable state and refuse unknown. Any override must be explicit and documented, not automatic. Ship independently of A6; admission is required by week 3.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Recorded fixtures distinguish an actual unsent draft, an empty prompt, a faint Claude suggestion, a dialog and unrecognized content. Faint suggestions alone are not classified as a human draft; draft contents are absent from the response.
2. A send targeting a detected draft or dialog refuses before any payload or submit reaches the PTY, with a machine-readable reason. A supported empty-prompt fixture accepts the existing send semantics.
3. Inspection uses the active screen even when the operator has scrolled upward. Cold/unattached tabs and unsupported prompt versions return unknown/unavailable rather than empty.
4. A controlled target close/replacement between inspection and dispatch does not send to another tab. A concurrent human-input fixture records the check-to-use limitation; CLI/help makes no atomic-safe-to-type claim.
5. An older server lacking the inspection verb produces the documented compatibility outcome, visibly distinguishing unguarded delivery from checked delivery. No continuous polling or input capture is introduced.

## Validation
Use recorded styled-screen parser fixtures, CLI tests with a fake socket that records whether a write occurred, and tests_v2 against a tagged app for actual draft/empty/dialog/cold-tab behavior. A computer-use pass types a real unsent draft and invokes send from another tab. Run an on-demand inspection/typing-latency soak on Atlas against F2. Do not test only source snippets.

Builds and soaks run on Atlas once F1 / C11-216 lands, through the build lock. Use a tagged artifact and its socket, launched with C11_QA_LAUNCH=fresh (or the tagged automation launcher); never an untagged DEV app. Record exact artifact/head and distinguish fixture assertions from the real product pass. Update affected CLI/event skill contracts, run scripts/sync-installed-skills.sh for edited installable skills and verify the installed copy.

## Dependencies
No mandatory in-workstream predecessor. Coordinate send response/error semantics with C3 and cold-tab inspection with H-D / C11-235; unknown is an allowed result, not an excuse to target a different tab. F1 / C11-216 supplies builds and F2 the measurement baseline. A6 depends on this. P2: individually releasable and admitted by week 3.

## Risks
Upstream’s styled grid is richer than plain read-screen; the delegator must confirm a viable c11 seam before promising broad provider support. Check-to-use races remain. Keep the S-to-M backlog estimate at M and escalate scope rather than building a generic classifier. Keep telemetry parsing, I/O, deduplication and sorting off main; apply only the minimal UI mutation asynchronously. Preserve the hitTest pointer guard, TabItemView equality boundary and allocation-free forceRefresh path. No tenant config writes or trust broadening. Localize new product strings in English plus ja, uk, ko, zh-Hans, zh-Hant and ru; validate interpolation tokens. Sanitize fixtures, screenshots and logs before inclusion in this public repository.

Size: M. Tier: P2. Doctrine check: optional per-process observation and explicit operator actions only; no blocking bridge, automatic approval or persistent tenant configuration.
data.title: Send: inspect styled prompt input and guard against overwriting operator drafts

data.body:
Codex takeover verification by agent:codex-feed against 0ff8887e5e965400b01645ef40b85fd0b2605cf2.

Replaced insufficient cursor-row style capture with a bounded complete prompt-region seam for wrapped drafts and multi-row dialogs; made native-lock/GhosttyKit and C11-257 barriers explicit; preserved unknown/older-server compatibility without redirecting closed targets.

Read owner-common/feed/takeover/run-state, the ticket and stored plan, the settled C11-272/C11-273 contract and named whole-plan audit findings. Checked cited c11 source and, for the native seam, pinned Ghostty 26c3e499ed8c4d65e3748248de7fd04c1e9a8103. Existing unread-navigation audit amendments remain intact. No human decisions opened. This is static planning evidence only: no builds, tests, UI launch, product edits, commits or pushes. Implementation remains on HOLD until Orchestrator BUILD MODE and each ticket's merged dependency gates.
